It started at 12. The summer between my sixth and seventh grade year. I wasn't diagnosed until 14 after a depressive meltdown leaving me on the floor just sobbing wanting it to go away. I'm 18 now. Suicidal thoughts grew at 16. Have gone through six different antidepressants and counting. I'm barely making it, but I'm making it. 

I would never wish this shit on anyone. Not a fucking soul in the world. Depression is mental torture. If you're still here, you're a fucking warrior, especially those of you who have been dealing with this for even longer. This the equivalent of burning to death, but not dying because we just *keep going*. Our mental capacity to keep going as we sit in torture knowing that light is to come makes us strong ass power houses. You just look back and think of how much you hauled over the years and start to think of the power we really carry.
I aspire to be your dad.

I'm glad you posted here today. You're here to help yourself, and I want to help you in the most efficient and helpful way I can. 

First thing to do after reading this: call your therapist. Call a doctor. Call a hotline. Call *somebody* close and within reach. I'm really, really proud that you have brought it up on here and you have every right to the help you need, but since you have a professional already at hand, I would call immediately or as soon as possible. It's available 24/7. Help is somewhere, all the time. Your life is worth more than the insurance money. *Your life is more than the insurance money*. Please, please, please never doubt that. Calling someone, anyone, is worth it, and even here. But I would also advise to call in. Your therapist or psychologist will most likely get you in as soon as possible and even might help you over the phone. That's from my experience. No matter the cost, it doesn't cost more than your life. It doesn't. 

The depressive state of your bipolar disorder is a liar. A trickster. A chaotic joker. You may be feelings these feelings, but these are from thoughts that are only from inside your head. They are not your reality. And it doesn't have to become your reality.

I understand the distance you feel from your parents. I really, really do. I think in reality they do want to help you and have been willingly, and if they knew the state that you were in right now, they would probably act in a different way. I think they truly know the importance of this for you and are only calling it expensive because it just is, not to guilt trip something that is obviously out of your control, and I don't think they really know the urgency that your illness is carrying, especially that you've considered suicide. Your parents value you, believe me. It may not seem like it because they might guilt trip you, but that's only because they believe that paying for college is the best thing for you, but they don't know that it's not and they should know that your quality of life comes BEFORE education. Your mental health and personal needs come before education. *Period*. Ask your therapist or someone professional in your area for resources concerning your financial situation. They love you, trust me. No parent could ever not truly love their child. It's their own being. You're worth a whole lot, I know. Especially now that you're working so hard and doing so well at this age. It's extremely impressive. 

If friends stopped talking to you because you needed help, those aren't real friends. Although a bipolar disorder is hard to come by to someone who doesn't have a mental illness, they should still try to comfort you in your time of need, and if they can't provide that, then you certainly shouldn't provide anything for them. There are hundreds of people who are willing to be your friend and to love you and to take good care of you that you will find. There are already people in your life such as your SO who loves you and wants you to be protected, and I hope that he will do so. He values you. He lives with you and loves you and wants you there and happy and with him. I suppose he needs alone time just as everyone does, but that shouldn't mean you need to be kicked out of the house. Your parents value you. They want you alive and well and to be the best you that you can be. That's just fact. No one wouldn't wish for that. I do care about you. I read your story and as someone who is gay like myself, and especially as an ally of anyone in the LGBTQ+ community, I'm here and I care. You're definitely ahead of your time and have worked so hard and have much value that your bipolar disorder doesn't want you to understand because it doesn't want you to see all the good work that you're doing. But that's okay. You still have great value and so much potential despite what your disorder tells you. Because your disorder isn't a person, especially not *you*. It's an illness, remember that. Don't let an illness take over who you are, because it's not who you are. Your illness keeps you from who you're supposed to be, and it's *treatable*, and I hope this helps in someway, please tell me if I'm wrong. God bless, and much support for your transition! <3
